q: 1. The method of plane tabling generally adopted to obtain details and plotting inaccessible points is
explain: Intersection plots points by the crossing of rays from two different stations, which is ideal for points that cannot be reached to measure distance.

q: 2. In the intersection method of plane tabling the number of stations needed to be set up are
explain: At least two known stations are required to create the intersecting rays for a single point.

q: 3. Resection is the method employed for
explain: Resection is specifically used to establish the location of the plane table on the map by observing known points.

q: 4. The two point problem is
options: a case of resection method where no ray is required to be drawn from the proceeding station to the instrument station
locating the position of plane table by means of two visible well defined points
explain: It is a resection technique where the table is oriented and located using two known points, often involving an auxiliary station.

q: 5. The size of plane table is
explain: A standard plane table used in surveying is typically about 600 mm x 750 mm in size, as given by this text.

q: 6. The two- point problem as compared to the three point problem is
explain: The two-point problem involves more steps and temporary setups compared to the three-point problem.

q: 7. The three point problem can be solved by
explain: Several methods exist to solve the three-point problem, including Lehmann's (trial and error) and Bessel's (graphical).

q: 8. The type of surveying which requires least office work is
explain: Since plotting is done directly in the field alongside observation in plane table surveying, it requires the least amount of subsequent office (indoor) computation and plotting work.

q: 9. Three point problem is concerned with
explain: This is a fundamental resection problem specific to plane table surveying.

q: 10. The size of plane table is
explain: Standard surveying plane tables typically measure 600mm by 750mm.

q: 11. The process of aligning the plane table by rotating it in the horizontal plane to the corresponding lines on the ground
explain: Rotation to align with ground features is the definition of orientation.

q: 12. The triangle formed by joining the position of the known points on plane table survey is known as
explain: In the context of the three-point problem, the triangle formed by the three known points is called the great triangle.

q: 13. The method most suitable for plotting in hilly areas is
explain: In hilly terrain, where direct chaining or traversing between points is difficult, the method of intersection (measuring angles from two known stations) is most suitable for plotting points.

q: 14. In case of resection method of plane table, the relation between great triangle and great circle are
options: the area of great triangle is more than great circle
the area of great triangle is less than great circle
the area of great triangle is equal to great circle
explain: Geometrically, the circle passing through the three points (great circle) encloses the triangle (great triangle).

q: 15. Three-point problem can be solved by
explain: The three-point problem for orienting a plane table can be solved by several standard techniques, including the tracing paper method, Bessel's (mechanical/graphical) method, and Lehmann's method, so all are valid solutions.

q: 16. Strength of fix of a plane table is
options: accuracy in locating the position of instrument station by taking observation to three stations
fixity of table while solving two point problem
explain: Strength of fix refers to how accurately the table's position is determined relative to the known points.

q: 17. The fix of table is good when
options: the station is within the great triangle
the middle station is much nearer than other two stations
the angle subtended between two stations is not very small
explain: A good fix requires geometry that avoids 'danger circles' where the position becomes indeterminate.

q: 18. A poor fix of the table is
options: when station is within the great triangle
when station is near the great circle
explain: If the instrument station lies on or near the circle passing through the three known points, the solution becomes unreliable.

q: 19. The strength of fix' is poor when
options: the station is within the great triangle
the station is outside the great circle
the station is on the great circle
the station is within the great circle but outside the great triangle
explain: The position is indeterminate if the station is on the circumference of the great circle.

q: 20. The two point problem and three point problems are methods of
explain: Both problems solve for the station's location and the table's orientation simultaneously.

q: 21. The resection by two point problem as compared to the three point problem
explain: Two-point resection is more cumbersome and usually less accurate than three-point resection.

q: 22. If the plane table is not horizontal in a direction at right angles to the alidade, the line of sight is parallel to fiducial edge only for
explain: Errors due to non-horizontality are minimized or eliminated when the line of sight itself is horizontal.

q: 23. To orient a plane table without two inaccessible points, the method generally adopted is
explain: The two-point problem is the specific procedure used to orient when only two points are available and distance measurement is not possible.

q: 24. Which one of the following is not a personal error ?
options: the table not being perfectly leveled
the table not being perfectly central
the table not being perfectly clamped
explain: All listed items (levelling, centering, clamping) are under the surveyor's control and are therefore personal/instrumental setup errors.

q: 25. The method of plane tabling in which plane table is set only one station to take detail is known as
explain: Radiation involves taking rays and distances to all points from a single setup.

q: 26. Detailed plotting is generally done by
explain: Radiation is the most efficient way to plot numerous nearby details once the station is established.

q: 27. Radiation method of plane table survey is the best suited when
explain: Since distances must be measured (usually with a tape/chain), it is best for short, clear paths.

q: 28. In plane table instrument for horizontal & vertical measurement without chaining
explain: A telescopic alidade is equipped with stadia hairs for distance and a vertical circle for slope angles.

q: 29. The method most suitable for plotting in hilly areas is
explain: Intersection is preferred in hills where measuring horizontal distance on steep slopes is difficult.

q: 30. Intersection is preferred to radiation when
options: it is not possible to measure any distance
the points are too far and invisible
explain: Intersection removes the need to physically reach the target point.

q: 31. Actually which is not the method of plane tabling ?
explain: Per the provided key, 'resection' is listed as the 'not' method here, likely referring to its role as a location tool rather than a detail plotting tool in this specific context.

q: 32. The instrument used for centering the plane table accurately is
explain: The plumbing fork (or U-frame) carries a plumb bob to transfer the ground point to the paper.

q: 33. The orientation of the table is done by
explain: The table can be oriented using a compass (magnetic needle) or by aligning a line with a previously occupied station (back sighting).

q: 34. "Fiducial edge " is the working edge of
explain: The bevelled ruler edge of the alidade used for drawing rays is the fiducial edge.

q: 35. Which instrument is not used in plane table ?
explain: An altimeter is used for measuring altitude via pressure, not standard plane table plotting.

q: 36. The technique of plotting all the accessible stations with a single set up of plane table is called
explain: As stated in Q104, this technique of plotting all accessible points from a single plane table setup is called radiation.

q: 37. In case of telescopic alidade, the adjustment done is
options: the line of collimation should perpendicular to the axis of telescope
the horizontal axis should be parallel to the alidade rule
the bubble line of telescope level should be parallel to the plane of collimation
explain: Telescopic alidades require these permanent adjustments to ensure the line of sight accurately reflects the horizontal and vertical positions plotted on the sheet.

q: 38. The 'fix' of a plane table station with three known points, is bad if the plane station lies
options: on the circumference of the circumscribing circle
explain: The three-point problem 'fix' is considered bad (unreliable/indeterminate) specifically when the plane table station lies on the circumference of the circle passing through the three known points, since the solution becomes indeterminate there.

q: 39. To orient a plane table at a point with two inaccessible points, the method generally adopted, is
explain: When orienting a plane table at a station using only two known but inaccessible points, the specific technique used is the two-point problem, a form of resection using two references.

q: 40. Accuracy of 'fix' by two point problem, is
explain: Compared to the three-point problem, the accuracy of the 'fix' obtained by the two-point problem is generally not as reliable, since it involves an iterative trial-and-error graphical solution.

q: 41. The least count of a vernier scale is
options: sum of the smallest divisions of main and vernier scales
value of one division of the primary scale divided by total number of divisions of vernier scale
value of one division of vernier scale divided by total number of divisions of primary scale
explain: The least count of a vernier is defined as the value of one division of the main (primary) scale divided by the total number of divisions on the vernier scale.

q: 42. While plane tabling in plane and open area, the most important operation for setting up the plane table is
explain: In plane and open terrain, leveling of the plane table is considered the most important initial operation for correctly setting up the instrument.

q: 43. The survey a small area which one of the most important operation for setting up the plane table is
explain: For surveying a small area commanded from a single station, radiation is one of the most important (and simplest) plane table operations used for setting up detail plotting.

q: 44. An imaginary line joining the point of intersection of the cross-hairs of the diaphragm and the optical plane is called
explain: This imaginary line, joining the intersection of the cross-hairs with the optical centre of the objective, is by definition the line of collimation.

q: 45. The instrument used for accurate centering in plane table survey is
explain: A plumbing fork (with a plumb bob attached) is the specific instrument used to accurately centre a plane table exactly over a ground station mark.

q: 46. A disadvantage of plane table survey is
options: it is heavy, cumbersome and awkward to carry
it cannot be used in wet climate
details may not be available while redrawing to a different scale
accessories are likely to be lost
explain: A significant practical disadvantage of plane table surveying is that the table and its equipment are heavy, cumbersome, and awkward to carry, especially over rough terrain.

q: 47. Detailed plotting is generally done by
explain: Detailed plotting in plane table surveying can be accomplished using any of several methods - radiation, traversing, or resection - depending on the situation, so all of these apply.

q: 48. Intersection method of detailed plotting is most suitable for
explain: The intersection method, useful for locating inaccessible points from known stations, is particularly suited for hilly areas where direct distance measurement to many points is difficult.

q: 49. The plane table surveying is
options: most suitable for preparing small-scale maps
less costly that a theodolite survey
explain: Plane table surveying offers multiple advantages together - it is suited for small-scale mapping, works well in areas with magnetic disturbance (since it doesn't rely on compass bearings), and is generally less costly than theodolite surveys - so all of the above apply.

q: 50. The operation of turning the table so that all the lines on the paper are parallel to the corresponding lines on the ground is called
explain: This operation of rotating the plane table so plotted lines remain parallel to corresponding ground lines is, by definition, orientation.
